descriptions.description: DATAPB is a data repository adhering to the CARE and FAIR principles of Open Science. Our repository is integrated into the National Open Science Consortium - CoNCiênciA/CNPq. DATAPB is co-funded by the Paraíba Research Support Foundation (FAPESQ-PB), the French Research Institute for Sustainable Development (IRD), and the Rectorate of the Federal University of Paraíba. The repository is managed by the Postgraduate Program in Ecology and Environmental Monitoring (PPGEMA, UFPB Campus IV) and maintained by a network of volunteer collaborators. Data of any format, area of ​​knowledge, and with any geographic or temporal scope can be deposited.

institutions.name: Fundação de Apoio à Pesquisa do Estado da Paraíba

descriptions.description:
The ELIXIR Luxembourg Data Catalogue is a unique collection of project-level metadata from large research initiatives in a diverse range of fields, including clinical, molecular and observational studies. Its aim is to improve the findability of these projects following FAIR data principles. 
The ELIXIR Luxembourg Data Sustainability Service, hosted by the Luxembourg Centre for Systems Biomedicine (LCSB) at the University of Luxembourg, offers a unique model for research data management. This service provides support for data hosting, access provision and findability, actively supporting the long-term availability, documentation, and regulatory compliance of datasets, platforms, and projects. Sustainability governance is integrated in the process by assisting data providers in defining access models, setting up Data Access Committees (DACs), and ensuring adherence to GDPR and relevant national legal frameworks. ELIXIR Luxembourg's role is operational and administrative: it stores and redistributes data under instruction of data providers, manages Data Use Agreements (DUAs), and coordinates user access requests and reporting. Access to data can be either open access (i.e., data can be accessed without restrictions) or controlled access, for which review by the provider-led DAC and signing of Data Use Agreement are required.

institutions.name: Luxembourg Centre for Systems Biomedicine, University of Luxembourg

descriptions.description: The CLARIAH-HiTZ is a repository that specializes in delivering language resources and technology mainly for the Basque language and Studies and also for the other official languages of Spain. It offers access to data and tools related to these areas on a sustainable basis and provides guidance to both users and developers. The repository provides sustainable long-term access to diverse linguistic resources including textual corpora, linguistically annotated corpora, lexical databases, dictionaries, natural language processing tools, Large Language Models and Digital Humanities applications.

institutions.name: Common Language Resources and Technology Infrastructure

descriptions.description: The Kyoto University Research Information Repository (KURENAI) offers online public access to Kyoto University's research and education materials, including in-house bulletins, dissertations, and academic journal articles. The Library Network has operated this system since 2006 to share Kyoto University's world-class intellectual products with society.

RADAR-BB offers researchers at publicly funded universities in Brandenburg a customized and user-friendly repository for archiving and publication of research data independent of discipline and format. The administration of the service is the responsibility of the service provider. The individual workflows for uploading, organising and annotating the research data with metadata as well as the curation of the datasets and optional quality assurance through peer review are the responsibility of the data provider. For data archiving, the retention period for data is 10 years and data providers can define access rights. Published datasets are kept for at least 25 years, they are always assigned a DOI via DataCite and can thus be internationally identified and cited. RADAR-BB is operated exclusively on servers in Germany. All contracts are subject to German law.

The Taalmaterialen (i.e. language resources) catalogue of the Dutch Language Institute (Instituut voor de Nederlandse Taal - INT) contains resources, data and tools for linguistic research and language and speech technology (LST) within the Dutch language area, such as text collections, word lists, scientific dictionaries, speech corpora and language and speech technology software.

BioTIME is a comprehensive collection of assemblage time-series in which the abundances of the species that comprise ecological communities have been monitored over time. The database is a free, publicly available, open-access resource.

EurOBIS - the European Node of the international Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS) - publishes distribution data on marine species, collected within European marine waters or collected by European researchers outside European marine waters.

An institutional repository where researchers at KTH Royal Institute of Technology can start using the repository as soon as you begin collecting and documenting data in your research. It allows you to document and archive your data and, when appropriate, choose to publish all or part of your research project’s data. You can document and submit different versions of your data and source code. A DOI can be reserved and data shared with reviewers via a secret link during the submission process of a manuscript to a journal.

names.name: University of Aruba Open Knowledge Repository

descriptions.description: The University of Aruba Open Knowledge Repository is the institutional repository managed by the University of Aruba Research Center. It contains research outputs such as data, software, publications, press releases and books.

The Publications of the Vienna University of Economics and Business system is a comprehensive research management system that not only serves as a continuously updated, extensive directory of researchers and research activities (e.g., publications, presentations, and projects) but also includes a repository and allows for the digital handling of third-party funding processes throughout the entire project lifecycle.

institutions.name: Vienna University of Economics and Business

descriptions.description:
CryoSeek represents a structure first paradigm for the discovery of biological entities. The CryoSeek strategy employs cryo electron microscopy (cryo EM) as a discovery tool to identify previously unknown biological entities directly isolated from natural environments or native resources. This approach is further integrated with AI facilitated computational tools and bioinformatic analyses to assess their potential origins and biological functions.
Remarkably, CryoSeek has uncovered numerous glycofibril structures, which have not been identified before. These findings suggest that CryoSeek may serve as a powerful strategy to explore the “dark matter” of the biological world.
The CryoSeek Database compiles the micrographs, 3D reconstructions, and atomic models of these biological “dark matters,” providing valuable resources to deepen our understanding of the natural world and to lay a foundation for the rational design of novel biomaterials.
The CryoSeek Database is developed, supported, and managed by Shenzhen Medical Academy of Research and Translation.

descriptions.description: This catalog allows users to deposit and/or access publicly available data and metadata from experiments and simulations provided by members of the scientific community. DOIs can be obtained and resolved and there are ample ways to access datasets. The metadata catalogue itself is based on Scicat and backed by a storage service based on dCache, everything hosted at DESY. All data available has been curated to the best effort and knowledge but is provided without warranty.

RADOGOST allows researchers to integrate, store, and access diverse archaeological datasets, including site reports, technical drawings, and specialist analyses, within a single standardized system. The platform enables advanced searching by chronology and location, providing a unified tool for managing dispersed documentation and facilitating data-driven syntheses.

The repository was established in 2015 and operates on software platform, which was developed and is maintained by the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Maribor (UM FERI).

descriptions.description:
Environmental related data and information are an important foundation for a sustainable development and need to be free, accessible, valid and transparent. 

The National Centre for Environmental and Nature conservation information at the German Federal Environment Agency (Umweltbundesamt – UBA) concentrates openly accessible data and information about the environment and nature conservation in its portal https://umwelt.info. We cooperate with data providers, identify relevant sources, reference their metadata and create target group specific editorials and tools. 

We want to counteract against the fragmented environmental data and information landscape in Germany. Our goal is to create one central, digital access point to all openly accessible data and information about the environment and nature conservation in Germany. We index this knowledge based on its metadata. We collect data and information from state agencies, science, business, and civil society. 

You can access our website here: https://umwelt.info/en.  

We provide our dataset via a RESTful API at https://md.umwelt.info/swagger-ui/#/ and an CKAN endpoint at https://md.umwelt.info/ckan

It provides long-term curation, preservation, and open dissemination of research data, including also  peer-reviewed publications, , technical reports, and associated research materials

institutions.name: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology

descriptions.description:
The aggregation of observations into a scientific repository aimed at quantifying the balance of greenhouse gases and climate uncertainties in the Amazon presents a unique opportunity to understand better how environmental phenomena operate in the region while enabling the synthesis of the enormous amount of data generated there. 
DataMap/Amazon was conceived with the above vision in mind. It is an initiative relevant to not only Brazilian but also Latin American science more generally, which typically lacks the necessary computational tools to integrate and synthesize knowledge from the vast collection of information by researchers from institutions such as the National Institute for Amazonian Research, the National Space Institute (INPE), USP, and the State University of Campinas.

institutions.name: Universidade de Sao Paulo, Escola Politécnica
University of São Paulo, Center for Sustainable Amazon Studies

descriptions.description: The Ocean Data Platform (ODP) gives ocean data scientists and researchers a single place to access, analyze, and share world ocean data — public, private, scientific, and industrial — in one unified environment. The integrated integrated catalog, user-controlled workspaces, and powerful APIs and SDKs enable advanced analytics, large-scale computation, and seamless cross-dataset harmonization. Collaborate with teams, publish high-quality datasets, and spend less time on data wrangling. Uniquely, the ODP unlocks industrial ocean data rarely available to researchers and will integrate high-resolution survey data from REV Ocean's state-of-the-art research vessel launching in 2027. The Ocean Data Platform is built by the non-profit HUB Ocean.

Open Causal functions as an open registry for FAIR causal graphs, where researchers can publish their graphs in machine-readable format with an open license and receive a DOI. Other researchers can search, comment, clone and modify existing graphs, fostering an open discussion on assumptions and enabling reuse of the models.

POLEN DataHub Repository is provided by FCCN, digital services FCT – Fundação para a Ciência e Tecnologia, with the aim of promoting the openness and sharing of data resulting from funded research, serving the national scientific community. This platform is aligned with Open Science practices and FAIR principles for research data management.

institutions.name: Fundação para a Ciência e Tecnologia

descriptions.description: data.THM is the institutional repository of Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen - University of Applied Sciences, where its researchers can publish research data and research software of any domain.

The Slovak Archive of Social Data (SASD), established in 2004, is a national repository dedicated to preserving and providing access to documentation and datasets from sociological and social science research in Slovakia. It archives data from major international programs such as ISSP, ESS, and EVS, as well as Slovak research projects funded by public, private, or commercial sources, provided they meet professional standards. SASD ensures long‑term accessibility of high‑quality social data for non‑commercial research, education, journalism, and public use, and also offers links to other international data archives and resources

Institute for Sociology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

descriptions.description: GERY, ie GEography RepositoRY is a joint digital repository of the all departments in University of Belgrade - Faculty of Geography. GERY provides open access to the publications, as well as to other outputs of the research projects implemented in this institution. The software platform meets the current requirements that apply to the dissemination of scholarly publications and it is compatible with relevant international infrastructures.

institutions.name: University of Belgrade - Faculty of Geography

descriptions.description: The Korea Sequence Read Archive (KRA) is a publicly available repository of high throughput sequencing data. KRA stores qualified raw sequencing data and alignment information and facilitates reproducibility through cloud-based data analysis service.

The Plant Adaptation Hub is a comprehensive web-based platform designed to empower scientists, farmers, and the general public with advanced tools and resources for Camelina research, farming, and exploration. This documentation provides an abstract knowledge of the key features which include:

the ability to perform genome-wide association studies (GWAS)
identify significant genetic variations
annotate genomic targets
visualization of genetic diversity (PCA and MDS)
visualization of phenotypic diversity
Please refer to Functional Modules on the left side column of this documentation for detailed exploration. The hub can be accessed at www.camelina-hub.org
For detailed documentation visit: https://usadellab.github.io/plant-adaptation-hub-documentation

Cupidon « Catalogue Unique pour le Partage Interopérable des DONnées » is the BRGM data repository. Metadata are moderated by community scientists before validation. Metadata are based on community standards (ISO 19115) and are exposed via standard API (CSW)

descriptions.description: A collection of Ground Truth data for handwritten and printed text recognition for South Asian scripts provided by FID4SA - Specialized Information Service South Asia. Researchers have the opportunity to download the data archived here and use it as training data for their own text recognition models. At the same time, researchers working on text recognition for South Asian scripts are invited to use this archive to make their own ground truth data available and to contribute to the creation of a ground truth data archive at a central site.

The Repository of Digital Objects for Teaching, Research and Culture ( RODERIC ) of the University of Valencia has the mission of preserving, organizing, disseminating and guaranteeing open access to the scientific, academic and cultural production generated by the university community. Its objective is to contribute to the consolidation of open, accessible and sustainable science, aligned with the principles of transparency, knowledge reuse and institutional commitment to society.

RODERIC responds to the commitment of the University of Valencia to the open access to knowledge movement, acquired with its adherence to the Berlin Declaration on Open Access to Knowledge in Sciences and Humanities (September 30, 2008), with the approval of the creation of the institutional repository by agreement of the Governing Council of the University of Valencia 195/2008 of the same day and with the approval of the Open Science Policy of the University of Valencia , in a session of the Governing Council of October 7, 2025.

The Mathematical Research Data Initiative (MaRDI) is part of Germany's national research data infrastructure (NFDI).
The MaRDI portal provides services to mathematicians from anywhere and supports them in discovering, documenting, and sharing mathematical research data. The MaRDI portal aggregates data from various sources and provides services for depositing research data.
Technically, the MaRDI portal is made with MediaWiki.

name: Repositório de Dados de Pesquisa UFG

names.name: Repositório de Dados de Pesquisa UFG

descriptions.description: RDP/UFG is the platform available for storing the research data of this institution. The purpose of the repository is to provide open access to data resulting from research conducted by members of the scientific community in various fields of knowledge, to raise the profile of the scientific output generated, to ensure the reproducibility of the research, and to preserve the data produced during the studies.

The Portuguese National Oceanographic Data Centre (NODC-PT) is a spatial data infrastructure (SDI) dedicated to the management and dissemination of marine geospatial data. It is part of a global network of national oceanographic data centres coordinated by the International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange (IODE) programme of the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC) of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).

The main objective of this infrastructure is to improve access to Portuguese marine data by promoting interoperable access to datasets that support scientific research and technical applications across several thematic domains, including atmospheric sciences, biological oceanography, chemical oceanography, marine geology, bathymetry, physical oceanography, environmental sciences, and administrative and reference data.

NODC-PT is jointly managed by the Hydrographic Institute (IH) and the Portuguese Institute for Sea and Atmosphere, I.P. (IPMA), in coordination with the Portuguese Committee for the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (CP-COI).

NODC-PT has been recognised as an endorsed action of the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (Ocean Decade), under Challenge 8: Create a Digital Representation of the Ocean.

Through this collaborative framework, NODC-PT facilitates the discovery, access, integration, and reuse of marine data, ensuring transparency and interoperability through the adoption of standardised metadata and international best practices.

The Indian Crop Phenome Database (ICPD), a domain of the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC) at the Regional Centre for Biotechnology, Faridabad, India, is developed for the sustainable archiving, management, and sharing of diverse crop phenome data generated across India. As a global agricultural powerhouse, India generates a significant portion of biological data, primarily from agricultural trials. However, much of this valuable data remains inaccessible, unpublished, and lost over time. ICPD addresses this gap by providing a user-friendly, centralized platform for freely archiving, organizing, analyzing, and sharing multi-crop phenome data in compliance with Minimum Information About a Plant Phenotyping Experiment (MIAPPE) and FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Re-usable) principles. Each dataset is assigned a unique, persistent IBDC accession. ICPD supports open and managed access submission modes. The database operates under a structured licensing framework (CC BY-NC-SA), ensuring proper attribution while encouraging ethical and non-commercial use of data.

NHLBI BioData Catalyst® (BDC) is a cloud-based ecosystem that offers researchers data, analytic tools, applications, and workflows in secure workspaces. It is a community where researchers can find, access, share, store, and analyze heart, lung, blood, and sleep data resources. And it is one of NHLBI’s data repositories, where researchers share scientific data from NHLBI-funded research so they and others can reproduce findings and reuse data to advance science. By increasing access to NHLBI data and innovative analytic capabilities, BDC accelerates reproducible biomedical research to drive scientific advances that can help prevent, diagnose, and treat heart, lung, blood, and sleep disorders.

institutions.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

descriptions.description:
ArmLifeBank is a FAIR-compliant biomedical data platform developed to centralize, preserve, and share research data generated by Armenian scientific laboratories. The platform integrates genomic, transcriptomic, clinical, and multi-omics datasets into a unified and interoperable infrastructure, increasing the visibility, accessibility, and reuse potential of Armenian biomedical research.

Built on the FAIRDOM-SEEK framework, ArmLifeBank supports standardized metadata annotation, persistent identifiers, and ontology-based organization to ensure interoperability with international scientific resources. The platform provides secure data management, collaborative research tools, and analytical pipelines for reproducible data analysis. By consolidating research outputs from diverse biomedical fields, including population genetics, hereditary diseases, cancer genomics, environmental health, and plant genomics, ArmLifeBank promotes open science, strengthens international collaboration, and supports the development of precision medicine approaches tailored to the Armenian population.

institutions.name: Institute of Molecular Biology, National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Armenia

name: Digitale Bibliothek der Erzbischöflichen Diözesan- und Dombibliothek Köln

names.name: Digitale Bibliothek der Erzbischöflichen Diözesan- und Dombibliothek Köln

descriptions.description: The Digital Library of the Archdiocese of Cologne and Cathedral Library contains mainly digitised medieval manuscripts from the Diocesan and Cathedral libraries, as well as historical books and incunabula from the historical collections of this library, focusing primarily on topics related to the Church of Cologne and its history. It spans a long period of Western European Christian and cultural history. In addition, you will find numerous publications from the institutional series ‘Libelli Rhenani’ and the journal ‘Analecta Coloniensia’ as well as recent publications by the Archdiocesan Vicariate General and its departments. The digital collections available here are continuously expanded and updated.

ARChive, based on InvenioRDM as its technological foundation, forms the core of a general data publication service for basic plant research. It supports the cultural shift toward the Open Data and Open Science principles agreed upon within the NFDI consortium by enabling the straightforward publication of large, non-textual data packages. The service integrates persistent identifiers from DataCite (DOIs), supports researchers in ensuring data quality, and guarantees long-term further development and compatibility with current storage and system environments through its modular and open design. Flexible, annotatable metadata improve discoverability, while the extensive REST API enables integration into existing workflows (e.g., Galaxy) and community-based curation processes without requiring new development.

The AMRDC Repository provides archival, preservation, and access services for Antarctic meteorological data, managing data from submission to end-user retrieval. The repository accepts datasets from accredited organizations and researchers engaged in research related to Antarctic meteorology and climatology. All datasets are made accessible to the larger Antarctic research community with metadata and publishing information for open-access use.

The TIB AV-Portal is an open-access platform for scientific videos and audio recordings, focusing on technology as well as architecture, chemistry, computer science, mathematics and physics. Over time, the scope of the portal has expanded to include a wider range of scientific disciplines, including the humanities and social sciences, economics, law and medicine (see subjects). Users of the portal have access to a diverse range of video and audio content, including lecture and conference recordings, simulations, animations, experiments, interviews and video abstracts as well as open educational resources.

The media stock of IWF Wissen und Medien gGmbH (1956 - 2011) was transferred to TIB in November 2012. This stock is not only made available for research in the TIB AV-Portal, but can also be used directly online, as far as possible, in the course of many years of measures for digitization, long-term archiving, indexing and rights clearance. This includes the ethnological film collection of IWF that is the largest in the world and comprises 1,953 films.

institutions.name: TIB – Leibniz Information Centre for Science and Technology and University Library

descriptions.description: Swinburne Figshare is an open access insitutional repository that hosts research data as well as manuscripts, media, commissioned reports, and other formats.

The ‘Deutsches Gedächtnis’ archive is the research data centre of the Institute for History and Biography at the FernUniversität in Hagen. It archives all interviews conducted since the early 1980s as part of contemporary history research and documentation projects at the Institute for History and Biography. In addition, collections of interviews from third-party research are incorporated. The archive is constantly growing through the Institute’s own projects, the incorporation of older collections from third parties, and support for ongoing external projects.
The interviews are life-history, narrative interviews in the style of oral history. They were conducted as part of contemporary history research projects as well as projects in qualitative sociological biographical research. They relate to socio-political events in Germany or to German history. The interviews originate predominantly from within Germany, but also from abroad, and are mainly in German; one in five interviews is in another language.
The interviews are made available for research, teaching and education in the form of audio or video recordings, transcripts, minutes/memos and short biographies, as well as information on the context of the research. A large proportion of the interviews are accessible online following registration and login. Researchers can search using full-text search and filter options.

institutions.name: FernUniversität in Hagen, Institut für Geschichte und Biographie

descriptions.description:
The LifeWatch ERIC Metadata Catalogue is a GeoNetwork-based platform for creating, managing and publishing metadata about resources related to biodiversity and ecosystem domain. Mainly built on the Ecological Metadata Language 2.2.0, ISO 19139 and European Open Science Cloud standards, it guarantees records are Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR). In doing so, it enables structured and standardised information to be openly available, promoting reuse, sharing, and integration by research communities, policymakers, and other stakeholders.

The Catalogue has already been adopted in several European projects and research initiatives, acting as a single access point for the discovery and access of tailored digital resources, increasing their visibility and findability.

EcoPortal is a repository of semantic artefacts for ecology and related domains. It has been developed by LifeWatch ERIC, in collaboration with its Italian node LifeWatch Italy coordinated by CNR, through the reuse of the OntoPortal technology to support the activities of different kinds of stakeholders (researchers, vocabularies managers, data managers, ontologists, etc.). EcoPortal assists the community in the creation, management, mapping, hosting, versioning, alignment, annotation, of semantic artefacts and subsequently also of its data, by adopting and fostering FAIR principles. It enables semantic interoperability by using well-known standards (e.g., SKOS, OWL, RDF, SPARQL, JSON, etc.). Ontologies can be explored across multiple federated portals (other OntoPortal instances i.e., AgroPortal, BioDivPortal and EarthPortal).

institutions.name: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche - Istituto di Ricerca sugli Ecosistemi Terrestri

name: Scientific Data Center of CAS Data Repository

names.name: Scientific Data Center of CAS Data Repository

descriptions.description:
The Scientific Data Center of CAS Data Repository is a research data repository for the Scientific Data Center of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. It supports the discovery, publication, access, and reuse of scientific data resources from CAS-related research activities and scientific data center workflows.

The repository provides resource search, metadata description, data access and download services, topic-based data collections, usage statistics, dataset-level licensing information, and persistent identifiers such as DOI and CSTR. It is powered by InstDB v3.0.1, an institutional data repository platform developed by the Computer Network Information Center, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CNIC, CAS).

institutions.name: Computer Network Information Center, Chinese Academy of Sciences

descriptions.description: RADAR4ING is a specialized repository for the NFDI4ING Community. It allows you to compile research data from completed scientific studies and projects into data packages, describe them with metadata, and make them publicly available. Published data receive a persistent identifier (DOI) and are thus discoverable internationally.

ArchaeoVault is a national repository for analytical archaeological data from the Czech environment and Czech archaeology. It mainly stores geospatial data, the results of laboratory analyses, anthropological data, 3D data, and databases. The repository is complementary to the Archaeological Information System of the Czech Republic and ensures FAIR principles: clear metadata, standardization, persistent identifiers, and connection to industry repositories. Data is curated for quality, long-term retention, and ease of reuse. The aim is to make research results available to experts, students, and institutions in one place.

MBLWHOI Library Dataverse is operated by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution Data Library and Archive. Its purpose is to store, share, and preserve scientific datasets, particularly those related to oceanographic and marine science research. It enables researchers to make their data publicly accessible, ensures long-term data stewardship, and supports reproducibility and transparency in scientific research.

The Research Vessel Observation Database provides the observational data acquired in the framework of the Joint Usage of Research Vessel program, including R/V Hakuho-Maru, Shinsei-Maru, Tansei-Maru, etc.
Users can also search  meta data of cruises and observations, CTD data, sample list, track and stations. Cruise details pages describe the cruise report, publication papers, and observation data files.

institutions.name: Atmosphere and Ocean Research Institute, The University of Tokyo

descriptions.description:
The Spanish Institute of Oceanography (IEO-CSIC), as Spain’s National Oceanographic Data Centre (NODC) within the International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange (IODE) network of the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC / UNESCO), manages, preserves and disseminates marine data and metadata generated through more than a century of oceanographic research. The IEO’s Oceanographic Data Centre was established in 1968 and has since played a key role in the management and international exchange of Spain’s oceanographic data. Its data resources cover a wide range of marine observations and oceanographic activities and are managed according to the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable).

The IEO geoportal, based on GeoNetwork and compliant with Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) Catalogue Service for the Web (CSW) and ISO 19115/19139 standards, provides access to a metadata catalogue (nodc.ieo.es/geonetwork) built primarily from SeaDataNet Cruise Summary Reports (CSR). It also offers geospatial visualisation and data access services, including Web Map Service (WMS) and Web Feature Service (WFS), and interactive dashboards for data exploration and analysis.

As a partner of SeaDataNet, the IEO contributes marine data and metadata through CSR and the Common Data Index (CDI), while also providing machine-to-machine access through CSW, Catalogue Service for the Web–Transactional (CSW-T), and a Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interface (REST API).

Research and Innovation Data at the DHBW.
The repository serves to make processed data from research and teaching projects at the DHBW available in accordance with the Open Science principle: ‘as open as possible, as closed as necessary’.

Historisch Centrum Limburg (HCL; in English: Historical Center Limburg) is a merger of the state repository in the capital of the province Limburg, the municipal repository of Maastricht and the municipal repository of Heerlen.

The municipalities of Heerlen and Maastricht, together with the national government, are the administrative partners in the Joint Regulation 'Gemeenschappelijke regeling Historisch Centrum Limburg 2020'. By this joint regulation, HCL is a public body and therefore a public-law organization.

HCL also has Service Agreements with: province of Limburg, water authority of Limburg, municipality of Beek, municipality of Beekdaelen, municipality of Brunssum, municipality of Eijsden-Margraten, municipality of Gulpen-Wittem, municipality of Landgraaf, municipality of Meerssen, municipality of Simpelveld, municipality of Vaals, municipality of Valkenburg aan de Geul, municipality of Voerendaal, and the joint regulations GGD Zuid-Limburg, Het Gegevenshuis, ISD Bol, Kompas, Gemeentelijk collectief voor werk, inkomen & zorg, Kredietbank Limburg, Omgevingsdienst Zuid-Limburg, Rd4, Stadsregio Parkstad, Veiligheidsregio Zuid-Limburg, het Werkgeversservicepunt Parkstad, het Werkvoorzieningschap Oostelijk Zuid Limburg, and Zorg- en Veiligheidshuis.

HCL collects, manages, and provides access to archives and collections of the aforementioned government institutions and private individuals and institutions in Limburg: those of religious communities, associations, foundations, companies, castles, families, and individuals. In principle, these archives are open to the public. In some cases, restrictions have been imposed to protect the privacy of living individuals. In addition to archives, HCL has extensive collections of manuscripts, almanacs, photographs, (land) maps, drawings, posters, prayer cards, and letterheads.

name: Digital Library of the University of Maribor

names.name: Digital Library of the University of Maribor

descriptions.description:
The Digital Library of the University of Maribor (DKUM) is the institutional repository of the University of Maribor and part of the Slovenian national open science infrastructure.
It provides preservation and access to research outputs produced at the University of Maribor, including research datasets from different disciplines, as well as theses, peer-reviewed publications, monographs, educational materials and other digital research objects.
Research data can be deposited by researchers and students of the University of Maribor and are subject to librarian-mediated validation. DKUM supports research data management in accordance with FAIR principles, the University of Maribor Open Science Policy and national open science requirements.

name: Repositorio Institucional de la Universidad Privada del Norte

names.name: Repositorio Institucional de la Universidad Privada del Norte

descriptions.description: The UPN Institutional Repository makes the academic and scientific output generated by the University's academic community available at both national and international levels, with the aim of contributing to research and sustainable development in society.
